title: Google /teamwork-LEAP Autonomously Formalizes the Weil Conjectures in 1.8M Lines of Lean 4
whyItMatters: First end-to-end machine-checked formalization of Pierre Deligne’s landmark 1974 Weil Conjectures—autonomously synthesized in 1.8M lines of Lean 4 alongside Hilbert’s 10th over rings, Birkhoff (1927), and 3D Bochner–Riesz.
summary: Unveiled by Google Research and Google Cloud AI on November 13, 2026, the multi-agent autoformalization system /teamwork-LEAP powered by Gemini 4 Argon fully autonomously produced an end-to-end machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Weil Conjectures—the foundational arithmetic-geometry theorems on zeta functions of algebraic varieties over finite fields proved by Pierre Deligne in 1974 (precursors to the Riemann Hypothesis). Spanning ~1.8 million lines of Lean generated across 28,800 subagent invocations, the same campaign also autonomously formalized a recent proof of Hilbert’s tenth problem over general rings of integers (919,000 lines), the 1927 Birkhoff Conjecture, and the 3D Bochner–Riesz Conjecture—catching and repairing a gap in an informal proof along the way.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously synthesized ~1.8 million lines of Lean 4 across 28,800 subagent invocations to formally verify the Weil Conjectures end-to-end.

Simultaneously delivered the first machine-checked formalizations of Hilbert’s 10th Problem over general rings of integers (919k lines), the 1927 Birkhoff Conjecture, and the 3D Bochner–Riesz Conjecture (fixing a gap in the informal proof).
Demonstrated context-partitioned multi-agent orchestration (Antigravity /teamwork + LEAP) capable of building massive modern algebraic-geometry formal libraries from informal literature.
caveats: Formalizes already-established landmark theorems (Deligne 1974) rather than solving an open conjecture, and independent algebraic geometers must still audit statement-level definitions across the 1.8M-line library to confirm full classical generality.

scoreRationale.foundational: Achieved autonomous machine verification of one of 20th-century mathematics’ deepest étale-cohomology and arithmetic-geometry edifices.
scoreRationale.ripple: Establishes reusable formal-verification infrastructure for arithmetic geometry and shows multi-agent formalizers can actively patch gaps in frontier informal papers.
scoreRationale.verification: Kernel-checked in Lean 4, scored slightly below human-audited Mathlib landmarks pending full external statement-fidelity review of the 1.8M-line codebase.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed what human formalization teams estimated as a multi-decade Mathlib effort into weeks across 28,800 autonomous subagent runs.
